cases.sentence: Разговор вертелся на той ___ из высшего управления, в которой большинство людей видит обыкновенно самый важный интерес внутренней политики.
cases.explain: «современной сплетне» — after the preposition «на», for location or topic.
cases.translation: The conversation turned on the contemporary gossip about those in power, in which most people see the chief interest of home politics. Denísov, dissatisfied with the government on account of his own disappointments in the service, heard with pleasure of the things done in Petersburg which seemed to him stupid, and made forcible and sharp comments on what Pierre told them.

cases.explain: «важный интерес» — the accusative marks the direct object of the verb.

cases.sentence: За расспросами этих двух собеседников разговор не выходил из этого ___ сплетни высших, правительственных сфер.
cases.explain: «обычного характера» — after the preposition «из», the genitive here marks possession, absence, or quantity.
cases.translation: Nikoláy, though free from Denísov’s readiness to find fault with everything, also thought that discussion of the government was a very serious and weighty matter, and the fact that A had been appointed Minister of This and B Governor General of That, and that the Emperor had said so-and-so and this minister so-and-so, seemed to him very important. And so he thought it necessary to take an interest in these things and to question Pierre. The questions put by these two kept the conversation from changing its ordinary character of gossip about the higher government circles.

cases.sentence: — Что̀ ж ___ могут сделать?
cases.explain: «честные люди» — the subject of the sentence stands in the nominative.
cases.translation: “What can decent men do?” Nikoláy inquired, frowning slightly. “What can be done?”

cases.sentence: Мужчины пошли в кабинет, и Николинька Болконский, незамеченный дядей, пришел туда же и сел в тени, к окну, у ___.
cases.explain: «письменного стола» — after the preposition «у», the genitive here marks possession, absence, or quantity.
cases.translation: Natásha, who had long expected to be fetched to nurse her baby, now heard the nurse calling her and went to the nursery. Countess Márya followed her. The men went into the study and Nikólenka Bolkónski followed them unnoticed by his uncle and sat down at the writing table in a shady corner by the window.

cases.sentence: — Вот что̀, — начал Пьер, не садясь и то ходя по комнате, то останавливаясь, шепелявя и делая ___ руками в то время, как говорил.
cases.explain: «быстрые жесты» — the accusative marks the direct object of the verb.
cases.translation: “Why this,” began Pierre, not sitting down but pacing the room, sometimes stopping short, gesticulating, and lisping: “the position in Petersburg is this: the Emperor does not look into anything. He has abandoned himself altogether to this mysticism” (Pierre could not tolerate mysticism in anyone now). “He seeks only for peace, and only these people sans foi ni loi136 can give it him—people who recklessly hack at and strangle everything—Magnítski, Arakchéev, and tutti quanti. … You will agree that if you did not look after your estates yourself but only wanted a quiet life, the harsher your steward was the more readily your object might be attained,” he said to Nikoláy.

cases.sentence: Цель прекрасная и всё; но в ___ надо другое.
cases.explain: «настоящих обстоятельствах» — after the preposition «в», for location or topic.
cases.translation: “Well, you know whom,” said Pierre, with a meaning glance from under his brows. “Prince Fëdor and all those. To encourage culture and philanthropy is all very well of course. The aim is excellent but in the present circumstances something else is needed.”

cases.sentence: Когда вы стоите и ждете, что вот-вот лопнет эта ___; когда все ждут неминуемого переворота, надо как можно теснее и больше народа взяться рука с рукой, чтобы противостоять общей катастрофе.
cases.explain: «натянутая струна» — the subject of the sentence stands in the nominative.
cases.translation: “Why? Let him be,” said Pierre, taking Nikoláy by the arm and continuing. “That is not enough, I told them. Something else is needed. When you stand expecting the overstrained string to snap at any moment, when everyone is expecting the inevitable catastrophe, as many as possible must join hands as closely as they can to withstand the general calamity. Everything that is young and strong is being enticed away and depraved. One is lured by women, another by honors, a third by ambition or money, and they go over to that camp. No independent men, such as you or I, are left. What I say is widen the scope of our society, let the mot d’ordre be not virtue alone but independence and action as well!”

cases.sentence: Оно не только не враждебное правительству, но это общество ___.
cases.explain: «настоящих консерваторов» — the genitive here marks possession, absence, or quantity.
cases.translation: “Why, the position of assistants. The society need not be secret if the government allows it. Not merely is it not hostile to government, but it is a society of true conservatives—a society of gentlemen in the full meaning of that word. It is only to prevent some Pugachëv or other from killing my children and yours, and Arakchéev from sending me off to some Military Settlement. We join hands only for the public welfare and the general safety.”

cases.sentence: Общество джентльменов в ___ этого слова.
cases.explain: «полном значении» — after the preposition «в», for location or topic.
cases.translation: “Why, the position of assistants. The society need not be secret if the government allows it. Not merely is it not hostile to government, but it is a society of true conservatives—a society of gentlemen in the full meaning of that word. It is only to prevent some Pugachëv or other from killing my children and yours, and Arakchéev from sending me off to some Military Settlement. cases.sentence: Мы только для того, чтобы Пугачев не пришел зарезать и моих и твоих детей, и чтоб Аракчеев не послал меня в военное поселение, — мы только для этого беремся рука с рукой, с одною целью ___ и общей безопасности.
cases.explain: «общего блага» — the genitive here marks possession, absence, or quantity.

Not merely is it not hostile to government, but it is a society of true conservatives—a society of gentlemen in the full meaning of that word. It is only to prevent some Pugachëv or other from killing my children and yours, and Arakchéev from sending me off to some Military Settlement. cases.sentence: — Да; но ___, следовательно враждебное и вредное, которое может породить только зло.
cases.explain: «тайное общество» — the subject of the sentence stands in the nominative.
cases.translation: “Yes, but it’s a secret society and therefore a hostile and harmful one which can only cause harm.”

cases.sentence: Еще более радостно-восторженно смотрел на Пьера забытый всеми мальчик, с тонкою шеей, выходившею из ___.
cases.explain: «отложных воротничков» — after the preposition «из», the genitive here marks possession, absence, or quantity.
cases.translation: The boy with the thin neck stretching out from the turndown collar—whom everyone had forgotten—gazed at Pierre with even greater and more rapturous joy. Every word of Pierre’s burned into his heart, and with a nervous movement of his fingers he unconsciously broke the sealing wax and quill pens his hands came upon on his uncle’s table.

cases.sentence: Всякое слово Пьера жгло его сердце и он ___ пальцев ломал, сам не замечая этого, — попадавшиеся ему в руки сургучи и перья на столе дяди.
cases.explain: «нервным движением» — the instrumental marks the means, company, or complement.
cases.translation: The boy with the thin neck stretching out from the turndown collar—whom everyone had forgotten—gazed at Pierre with even greater and more rapturous joy. Every word of Pierre’s burned into his heart, and with a nervous movement of his fingers he unconsciously broke the sealing wax and quill pens his hands came upon on his uncle’s table.

cases.sentence: — Совсем не то, что̀ ты думаешь, а вот что̀ такое было ___, и тот, который я предлагаю.
cases.explain: «немецкий тугендбунд» — the subject of the sentence stands in the nominative.
cases.translation: “It is not at all what you suppose; but that is what the German Tugendbund was, and what I am proposing.”

cases.sentence: Пьер доказывал противное и, так как его ___ были сильнее и изворотливее, Николай почувствовал себя поставленным в тупик.
cases.explain: «умственные способности» — the subject of the sentence stands in the nominative.
cases.translation: Pierre smiled, Natásha began to laugh, but Nikoláy knitted his brows still more and began proving to Pierre that there was no prospect of any great change and that all the danger he spoke of existed only in his imagination. Pierre maintained the contrary, and as his mental faculties were greater and more resourceful, Nikoláy felt himself cornered. This made him still angrier, for he was fully convinced, not by reasoning but by something within him stronger than reason, of the justice of his opinion.

cases.sentence: — Я вот что̀ тебе скажу, — проговорил он, вставая и ___ уставляя в угол трубку и наконец бросив ее.
cases.explain: «нервными движениями» — the instrumental marks the means, company, or complement.
cases.translation: “I will tell you this,” he said, rising and trying with nervously twitching fingers to prop up his pipe in a corner, but finally abandoning the attempt. “I can’t prove it to you. You say that everything here is rotten and that an overthrow is coming: I don’t see it. But you also say that our oath of allegiance is a conditional matter, and to that I reply: ‘You are my best friend, as you know, but if you formed a secret society and began working against the government—be it what it may—I know it is my duty to obey the government. And if Arakchéev ordered me to lead a squadron against you and cut you down, I should not hesitate an instant, but should do it.’ And you may argue about that as you like!”

cases.sentence: После этих слов произошло ___.
cases.explain: «неловкое молчание» — the subject of the sentence stands in the nominative.
cases.translation: An awkward silence followed these words. Natásha was the first to speak, defending her husband and attacking her brother. Her defense was weak and inapt but she attained her object. The conversation was resumed, and no longer in the unpleasantly hostile tone of Nikoláy’s last remark.

cases.sentence: Разговор снова возобновился и уже не в том неприятно ___, в котором сказаны были последние слова Николая.
cases.explain: «враждебном тоне» — the prepositional is used only after a preposition, for location or topic.
cases.translation: An awkward silence followed these words. Natásha was the first to speak, defending her husband and attacking her brother. Her defense was weak and inapt but she attained her object. The conversation was resumed, and no longer in the unpleasantly hostile tone of Nikoláy’s last remark.

cases.sentence: Разговор снова возобновился и уже не в том неприятно враждебном тоне, в котором сказаны были ___ Николая.
cases.explain: «последние слова» — the subject of the sentence stands in the nominative.
cases.translation: An awkward silence followed these words. Natásha was the first to speak, defending her husband and attacking her brother. Her defense was weak and inapt but she attained her object. The conversation was resumed, and no longer in the unpleasantly hostile tone of Nikoláy’s last remark.

cases.sentence: Мальчик нагнул голову и тут в ___ как будто заметил, что̀ он наделал на столе.
cases.explain: «первый раз» — after the preposition «в», the accusative marks the direct object of the verb.
cases.translation: The lad looked down and seemed now for the first time to notice what he had done to the things on the table. He flushed and went up to Nikoláy.
